narrative:
Based on the model’s assessment, your application was denied because you were found to represent an elevated credit risk. The model estimates that you have a 43% chance of becoming a bad credit risk, meaning that, in the bank’s view, there is a significant probability that you may struggle to repay the loan. While this is not a majority chance, it is high enough that the bank is not willing to take on that risk.

The most important factor in this decision was the length of the loan you requested. You asked to repay the credit over 48 months, which is more than twice the average duration of about 19 months among approved applicants. A longer repayment period means more time for financial circumstances to change, and the model sees this as a strong signal of increased risk. This single factor pushed most strongly toward denial.

Interestingly, two other factors actually worked in your favor. Your credit history, despite showing past delays, was not as problematic as other possible credit histories, so it slightly lowered your estimated risk. Similarly, your employment situation, while currently unemployed, did not add to the risk according to the model; in fact, it nudged the prediction toward a better outcome. However, these positive influences were not enough to outweigh the impact of the very long loan duration.

To improve your chances in the future, consider requesting a smaller loan with a much shorter repayment period, ideally closer to the average. Also, demonstrating a stable income, even part-time, and addressing any past credit issues would help strengthen your application. Speaking with a bank advisor about these options may give you a clearer path forward.
